The boycott mentioned in the fifth paragraph refers to the Swadeshi movement’s call to boycott foreign cloth and promote spinning and weaving in India.  
The Great Depression that started in 1929 weakened the British economy and reduced its ability to maintain colonial control, making colonial markets less profitable and increasing the economic pressure from Indian boycotts.  
This economic strain helped the Indian independence movement gain leverage in later years.  

Final answer: (B)
